content:
incident-bot: PAGING: gpu-pool-pending alert triggered (backlog 920). autoscaler failing to add GPU nodes. paging sre_oncall @jamie :rotating_light:

jamie: on it. seeing huge queue on inference-queue. pulling autoscaler logs now.

carla: customers reporting elevated 503s on /v1/generate, some retries succeeding. can we triage impact and SLOs?

jamie: quick status: queue ~1100 waiting tokens, token_throttle engaged, 30% tail latency increase. autoscaler logs showing repeated launch template validation errors -> nodes not provisioning. grabbing CA logs: 

jamie: ```
I0210 14:05:12 autoscaler.go:204] ScaleUp: need 12 nodes for GPU workload
E0210 14:05:13 awsprovider.go:422] create ASG failed: InvalidLaunchTemplateVersion: The specified value for LaunchTemplateVersion does not exist.
status code: 400, request id: 1234-abc
E0210 14:05:14 autoscaler.go:278] Failed to scale up: launch template validation failed
```

leo: that matches recent config drift after the rollout yesterday where we updated the gpu-launch-template to v5. some nodegroups still reference v4.

maria: also seeing IAM errors in cloudtrail for the autoscaler role: ```AccessDenied: iam:PassRole denied for role arn:aws:iam::acct:role/eks-node-role-v5``` Possible role rename during rollout.

ash: quick mitigation suggestion: 1) revert template pointer on affected nodegroups to the previous valid version, or 2) create a temporary nodegroup with known-good template and taint/wait, then cordon/evict. Which is faster?

jamie: temp nodegroup might be fastest. but autoscaler is blocked so manual nodegroup create via eksctl or console is our path. I'll start a manual create with template v4 and label it gpu-emergency-xx.

carla: prep messaging to support: tell customers we're mitigating and routing critical production tenants to fallback CPU model for short-term. Sam, can product pick highest-priority tenants?

sam: yes, listing top 6 paying tenants. will DM support the list now so we can move them to fallback targets.

jamie: started eksctl create nodegroup --cluster=prod --name=gpu-emergency-1 --node-type=p4d --launch-template=lt-0abcd:v4 --node-labels=inference=gpu-emergency --taints=special/gpu:NoSchedule

incident-bot: deploy-bot: started provisioning nodegroup gpu-emergency-1 (request id eg-5678). ETA ~8-12m.

leo: while that's provisioning, reduce queue pressure by throttling noncritical batch jobs. ash can we pause nightly retrains and background evals?

ash: pausing experiment queues now. kubectl scale deployment eval-workers --replicas=0 --namespace=jobs 

jamie: new nodegroup coming up: nodes joining but showing NotReady due to kubelet bootstrap failing with taint mismatch. checking kubelet logs.

jamie: kubelet error: ```NodeBootstrap: unable to attach IAM role to instance: UnauthorizedOperation: iam:PassRole denied for role arn:aws:iam::acct:role/eks-node-role-v4```

maria: looks like the instance profile for v4 was deleted in cleanup script last week. Ops must reattach or we need to create a new instance profile with proper trust policy.

leo: ops, can you attach the instance profile gpu-node-profile-v4 to the launch template or update LT to reference the profile that still exists?

carla: meanwhile I'm drafting customer status: "We are experiencing increased latency and intermittent 503s for GPU-backed inference. We are provisioning emergency GPU capacity and routing critical tenants to CPU fallback. ETA for capacity restoration ~30 minutes." Posting to status.redwood.ai/incidents.

jamie: manual fix: created new instance profile gpu-node-profile-temp, attached necessary roles, updated LT via API to set InstanceProfile to gpu-node-profile-temp, re-created nodegroup. nodes now coming Ready.

incident-bot: monitor-bot: Observability: GPU pool capacity recovered from 8 to 20 nodes over 18 minutes. queue decreasing to 220. token_throttle reduced.

sam: customers rerouted to CPU fallback are reporting degraded throughput but no errors. thanks for quick mitigation.

ash: next: drain a few noisy tenants from GPU pool to free cache / KV pressure, and enable prefix cache warmup on new nodes.

jamie: draining low-priority pods now: kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data.

carla: taking notes for postmortem: root cause (launch template version mismatch + instance profile cleanup), contributing factor (deploy rollout changed template versions without updating nodegroups), impact (elevated 5xx and throttles for ~35m), mitigation (manual nodegroup + instance-profile recreate, fallback routing), timeline, owners.

leo: opening a ticket to add a CI check for launch-template references and to prevent automated cleanup of instance profiles tied to active LTs. assigning to eng-infra.

jamie: handing off to carla for 4h follow-up. I'll be on standby for rollback if anything regresses.

carla: taking over at 15:20 UTC. thanks jamie. incident-bot schedule: postmortem draft reminder in 24h and attach logs. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: NOTE: thread archived in 48h unless flagged.
